title: EvalPulse: contextual alert throttling and consolidated channel cards for regression notices
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Background: We get frequent eval regressions after config/model changes. Operators and SREs are flooded with duplicated Slack threads and PagerDuty pages for correlated failures (same prompt set / model variant), making it hard to triage and increasing noise. Current Console alerts are per-eval-run and do not collapse similar events or provide contextual change attribution.

Goal: Deliver a Console-first feature (EvalPulse) that: 1) consolidates related eval regression alerts into a single channel card with clear attribution to the triggering change (model version, quantization, batching/config), 2) applies configurable contextual throttling to limit noisy duplicates, and 3) integrates with Slack and PagerDuty with compact payloads and explicit links back to the eval diff and rollout controls.

Non-goal: Do not change core runtime rollbacks or automatic model fallback policies in this ticket; we will only expose notifications and controls in Console.

Success metrics: reduction in total Slack threads from eval regressions by 60% in first 30 days, reduction in redundant PagerDuty pages by 70%, median time-to-acknowledge for regression pages reduced by 20% because of clearer attribution, and NPS (internal) for operators > 4.0 on the new alert UX.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows a single consolidated EvalPulse card for groups of regression events that are within the same change window (config/model change) and match similarity rules

Slack messages use a compact card with 1) summary verdict (severity), 2) top 3 failing prompts with short diffs, 3) attribution to change (model version/commit/config diff), and 4) single buttons: Open Eval, Acknowledge, Create Incident
PagerDuty pages created only for high-severity consolidated events; duplicate triggers within 30m are suppressed unless severity increases
Config UI in Console lets teams define dedupe windows (default 30m), matching keys (prompt-set, model-family, dataset-id), and severity thresholds
Audit trail accessible from card linking to eval-run ids, model artifact version, and the Console rollout that triggered the change
Backend exposes telemetry: counts of suppressed alerts, grouped event rate, and false-suppression rate; dashboards created in Console telemetry workspace
E2E test covering: change triggers eval -> grouped event appears in Console -> Slack card sent -> PagerDuty page sent when severity threshold met
